title.zh: 卷二百〇八 列傳第九十五: 外夷一 高麗 耽羅 日本
title.en: Volume 208 Biographies 95: Foreign Peoples 1 - Goryeo, Tamna, Japan
title.raw: 卷二百〇八 列傳第九十五: 外夷一 高麗 耽羅 日本 Volume 208 Biographies 95: Foreign Peoples 1 - Goryeo, Tamna, Japan

sentences.zh: 高麗本箕子所封之地，又扶餘別種嘗居之。

translations.literal: Goryeo was originally the land enfeoffed to Jizi; moreover a separate branch of Buyeo once dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo was originally the domain granted to Jizi, and a distinct offshoot of Buyeo had also settled there.

sentences.zh: 其地東至新羅，南至百濟，皆跨大海，西北度遼水接營州，而靺鞨在其北。

translations.literal: Its territory extended east to Silla and south to Baekje, both across the great sea; northwest it crossed the Liao River to join Ying Prefecture, and Mohe lay to its north.
translations.idiomatic: Its lands reached east to Silla and south to Baekje, both beyond the open sea; to the northwest it crossed the Liao River to meet Ying Prefecture, with Mohe to the north.

sentences.zh: 其國都曰平壤城，即漢樂浪郡。

translations.literal: Its national capital was called Pyongyang City—that is, the Han dynasty's Lelang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was Pyongyang, the site of the Han dynasty's Lelang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 水有出靺鞨之白山者，號鴨淥江，而平壤在其東南，因恃以為險。

translations.literal: Waters issuing from White Mountain in Mohe were called the Yalu River; Pyongyang lay to its southeast, and they relied on this as a defense.
translations.idiomatic: A river rising from White Mountain in Mohe was known as the Yalu; Pyongyang stood to its southeast, and the kingdom counted on it for protection.

sentences.zh: 後辟地益廣，并古新羅、百濟、高句麗三國而為一。

translations.literal: Later they opened territory ever wider, merging the three ancient states of Silla, Baekje, and Goguryeo into one.
translations.idiomatic: Later its frontiers expanded until the three former kingdoms of Silla, Baekje, and Goguryeo were united under one rule.

sentences.zh: 其主姓高氏，自初立國至唐乾封初而國亡。

translations.literal: Its rulers bore the surname Gao; from the founding of the state until the beginning of the Qianfeng era in Tang, the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: Its kings were of the Gao clan; the state endured from its founding until it fell in the early Qianfeng period of Tang.

sentences.zh: 垂拱以來，子孫復封其地，後稍能自立。

translations.literal: Since the Chuigong era, descendants were again enfeoffed there, and later they gradually regained autonomy.
translations.idiomatic: From the Chuigong reign onward their descendants were re-enfeoffed in the land, and in time they gradually regained self-rule.

sentences.zh: 至五代時，代主其國遷都松岳者，姓王氏，名建。

translations.literal: By the Five Dynasties period, the one who replaced the ruler of the state and moved the capital to Songak bore the surname Wang; his name was Geon.
translations.idiomatic: In the Five Dynasties period the man who supplanted the throne and moved the capital to Songak was Wang Geon of the Wang clan.

sentences.zh: 自建至燾凡二十七王，歷四百餘年未始易姓。

translations.literal: From Geon to Yeol there were twenty-seven kings in all, spanning more than four hundred years without a change of surname.
translations.idiomatic: From Wang Geon to Wang Yeol there were twenty-seven kings in all, and for more than four hundred years the ruling surname never changed.

sentences.zh: 入元，太祖十一年，契丹人金山、元帥六哥等領衆九萬餘竄入其國。

translations.literal: Under the Yuan, in the eleventh year of Taizu, the Khitan men Jinshan, Marshal Liuge, and others led a host of more than ninety thousand who fled into their country.
translations.idiomatic: After entering the Yuan era, in the eleventh year of Taizu, the Khitan leaders Jinshan and Marshal Liuge led a force of more than ninety thousand who fled into Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 十二年九月，攻拔江東城據之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twelfth year they stormed and took Jiangdong Fortress and held it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the twelfth year they captured Jiangdong Fortress and occupied it.

sentences.zh: 十三年，帝遣哈只吉、劄剌等領兵征之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Emperor dispatched Hazhiji, Zhala, and others to lead troops in campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Emperor sent Hazhiji, Zhala, and others at the head of an army to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 國人洪大宣詣軍中降，與哈只吉等同攻圍之。

translations.literal: The countryman Hong Daxuan came to the army and surrendered, joining Hazhiji and the others in investing the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: A Goryeo subject, Hong Daxuan, came to the camp and submitted, then joined Hazhiji and the others in besieging the Khitan force.

sentences.zh: 高麗王名缺奉牛酒出迎王師，且遣其樞密院使、吏部尚書、上將軍、翰林學士承旨趙沖共討滅六哥。

translations.literal: The Goryeo king, named Que, brought oxen and wine out to welcome the imperial army, and also sent his privy councilor, minister of personnel, supreme general, and Hanlin academician ex officio Zhao Chong to join in destroying Liuge.
translations.idiomatic: King Goryeo Wang Gyu brought oxen and wine to welcome the imperial troops and sent his privy councilor, minister of personnel, supreme general, and Hanlin academician ex officio Zhao Chong to help exterminate Liuge.

sentences.zh: 劄剌與沖約為兄弟。

translations.literal: Zhala and Chong swore brotherhood with each other.
translations.idiomatic: Zhala and Zhao Chong pledged brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 沖請歲輸貢賦。

translations.literal: Chong requested that tribute be submitted annually.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chong asked that annual tribute be paid.

sentences.zh: 劄剌曰：「爾國道遠，難於往來，每歲可遣使十人入貢。

translations.literal: Zhala said: "Your country lies far away and travel is difficult; each year you may send ten envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Zhala said, "Your country is distant and hard to reach; each year you may send ten envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 」十二月，劄剌移文取兵糧，送米一千斛。

translations.literal: " In the twelfth month Zhala sent a formal communication requesting military grain; they delivered one thousand piculs of rice.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twelfth month Zhala requisitioned military provisions, and they sent one thousand piculs of rice.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，遣其權知閤門祗候尹公就、中書注書崔逸以結和牒文送劄剌行營，劄剌遣使報之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year they sent the acting custodian of the Gate Attendants' Office Yin Gongjiu and Secretariat clerk Cui Yi with a treaty memorandum to Zhala's field headquarters; Zhala dispatched envoys in reply.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourteenth year they sent Acting Gate Attendant Yin Gongjiu and Secretariat clerk Cui Yi with a peace memorandum to Zhala's camp, and Zhala sent envoys in response.

sentences.zh: 高麗王以其侍御史朴時允為接伴使迎之。

translations.literal: The Goryeo king appointed his attendant censor Pak Siyun as welcoming commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Goryeo king appointed his attendant censor Pak Siyun commissioner to receive them.

sentences.zh: 帝又遣蒲里也持詔往諭之，高麗王迎拜設宴。

translations.literal: The Emperor also sent Puliye bearing an edict to instruct them; the Goryeo king received him with bowing and held a feast.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also sent Puliye with an edict to instruct them; the Goryeo king received him with obeisance and held a banquet.

sentences.zh: 九月，皇太弟、國王及元帥合臣、副元帥劄剌等各以書遣宣差大使慶都忽思等十人趣其入貢，尋以方物進。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Imperial Younger Brother, the king, and the marshals Hechen, Vice-Marshal Zhala, and others each sent letters by the ten commissioners of distinction Qingduhusi and the rest urging tribute; shortly thereafter they presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Imperial Younger Brother, the king, and the marshals Hechen and Vice-Marshal Zhala each sent letters by ten commissioners, including Qingduhusi, urging tribute; local products soon followed.

sentences.zh: 十五年九月，大頭領官堪古苦、著古歟等復以皇太弟、國王書趣之，仍進方物。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifteenth year the grand headmen Guanguku, Zhugu'er, and others again urged them with letters from the Imperial Younger Brother and the king, and again presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fifteenth year the grand headmen Guanguku and Zhugu'er again pressed them with letters from the Imperial Younger Brother and the king, and again sent local products.

sentences.zh: 十六年七月，有旨，諭以伐女直事，始奉表陳賀。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixteenth year an order was issued instructing them regarding the campaign against the Jurchen; they then submitted a congratulatory memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixteenth year an imperial order informed them of the campaign against the Jurchen, and they at last submitted a congratulatory memorial.

sentences.zh: 八月，著古歟使其國。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Zhugu'er was sent to their country.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Zhugu'er was dispatched to their country.

sentences.zh: 十月，喜速不瓜等繼使焉。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Xisubugua and others followed as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Xisubugua and others were sent in succession.

sentences.zh: 十七年十月，詔遣著古歟等十二人至其國，察其納款之實。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the seventeenth year an edict dispatched Zhugu'er and eleven others to their country to investigate the reality of their submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the seventeenth year an edict sent Zhugu'er and eleven others to Goryeo to verify whether their submission was genuine.

sentences.zh: 十八年八月，宣差山朮等十二人復以皇太弟、國王書趣其貢獻。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eighteenth year the commissioners of distinction Shanzhu and eleven others again urged tribute with letters from the Imperial Younger Brother and the king.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the eighteenth year the commissioners Shanzhu and eleven others again pressed for tribute with letters from the Imperial Younger Brother and the king.

sentences.zh: 十九年二月，著古歟等復使其國；

translations.literal: In the second month of the nineteenth year Zhugu'er and others were again sent to their country;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the nineteenth year Zhugu'er and others were again sent to their country;

sentences.zh: 十二月，又使焉，盜殺之于途，自是連七歲絕信使矣。

translations.literal: in the twelfth month envoys were sent again; bandits killed them on the road, and from then on no messengers came for seven years straight.
translations.idiomatic: in the twelfth month another mission was sent, but bandits killed them on the road; for seven years thereafter no envoys passed between the two courts.

sentences.zh: 太宗三年八月，命撒禮塔征其國，國人洪福源迎降于軍，得福源所率編民千五百戶，旁近州郡亦有來師者。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Taizong, Salitai was ordered to campaign against their country; the countryman Hong Fuyuan came to the army and surrendered, yielding the fifteen hundred registered households under Fuyuan's command, and nearby prefectures and districts also had men who came to the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Taizong's third year Salitai was ordered to campaign against Goryeo; Hong Fuyuan came out to the army and submitted, bringing fifteen hundred registered households, and neighboring districts also sent men to join the invaders.

sentences.zh: 撒禮塔即與福源攻未附州郡，又使阿兒禿與福源抵王京，招其主王，遣其弟懷安公王侹請和，許之。

translations.literal: Salitai then joined Fuyuan in attacking still-unsubmitted prefectures and districts, and also sent Aritu and Fuyuan to the royal capital to summon the king Wang; he sent his younger brother the Duke of Huai'an Wang Yan to sue for peace, which was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Salitai then joined Fuyuan in reducing unsubmitted prefectures, and sent Aritu and Fuyuan to the royal capital to summon King Wang; the king sent his younger brother, the Duke of Huai'an Wang Yan, to sue for peace, and peace was granted.

sentences.zh: 置京、府、縣達魯花赤七十二人監之，遂班師。

translations.literal: Darughachi were installed in seventy-two capital, prefecture, and county posts to oversee them, and the army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-two darughachi were posted in the capital, prefectures, and counties to supervise them, and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十一月，元帥蒲桃、迪巨、唐古等領兵至其王京，遣使奉牛酒迎之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the marshals Putao, Diju, Tanggu, and others led troops to the royal capital; envoys were sent bearing oxen and wine to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the marshals Putao, Diju, and Tanggu led troops to the royal capital, and envoys came out with oxen and wine to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 十二月一日，復遣使勞元帥于行營。

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month envoys were again sent to comfort the marshals at their camp.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the twelfth month envoys were again sent to visit the marshals in camp.

sentences.zh: 明日，其使人與元帥所遣人四十餘輩入王城，付文牒。

translations.literal: The next day their envoys and more than forty men sent by the marshals entered the royal city and delivered documents.
translations.idiomatic: The next day their envoys and more than forty men sent by the marshals entered the royal city and exchanged documents.

sentences.zh: 又明日，遣王侹等詣撒禮塔屯所犒師。

translations.literal: Again the next day Wang Yan and others were sent to Salitai's encampment to reward the troops.
translations.idiomatic: On the day after that Wang Yan and others were sent to Salitai's camp to reward the army.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，帝遣使以璽書諭。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year the Emperor dispatched envoys bearing an imperial letter under seal to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year the Emperor sent envoys with a sealed imperial letter of instruction.

sentences.zh: 三月，遣中郎將池義源，錄事洪巨源、金謙等齎國贐牒文送撒禮塔屯所。

translations.literal: In the third month the Central Lieutenant Chi Ewon, registrar Hong Geunwon, Jin Qian, and others were sent carrying state credentials and documents to Salitai's camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Central Lieutenant Chi Ewon and the registrars Hong Geunwon and Jin Qian were sent with state credentials to Salitai's camp.

sentences.zh: 四月，遣其將軍趙叔昌、御史薛慎等奉表入朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth month their general Zhao Shuchang, censor Xue Shen, and others presented a memorial to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month they sent their general Zhao Shuchang, censor Xue Shen, and others to court with a memorial.

sentences.zh: 五月，復下詔諭之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month an edict was again issued instructing them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month another edict was issued to instruct them.

sentences.zh: 六月，盡殺朝廷所置達魯花赤七十二人以叛，遂率王京及諸州縣民竄海島。

translations.literal: In the sixth month they killed all seventy-two darughachi installed by the court in rebellion, then led the people of the royal capital and all prefectures and counties to flee to sea islands.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month they slaughtered all seventy-two court-appointed darughachi in revolt, then led the people of the capital and the prefectures to flee to the islands.

sentences.zh: 洪福源集餘民保聚，以俟大兵。

translations.literal: Hong Fuyuan gathered the remnant people to hold out, awaiting the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Fuyuan gathered the remaining people into fortified settlements to await the main army.

sentences.zh: 八月，復遣撒禮塔領兵討之，至王京南，攻其處仁城，中流矢卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Salitai was again sent leading troops to punish them; reaching south of the royal capital, he attacked their Choin Fortress and died of an arrow wound.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Salitai was again sent to punish them; reaching south of the royal capital he attacked their Choin Fortress and was killed by an arrow.

sentences.zh: 別將鐵哥以軍還。

translations.literal: The lieutenant general Tiege led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Lieutenant general Tiege withdrew the army.

sentences.zh: 其已降之人，令福源領之。

translations.literal: Those who had already surrendered were placed under Fuyuan's command.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had already submitted were placed under Fuyuan's command.

sentences.zh: 十月，遣其將軍金寶鼎、郎中趙瑞章上表陳情。

translations.literal: In the tenth month they sent their general Jin Baoding and supervising secretary Zhao Ruizhang to submit a memorial stating their case.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month they sent their general Jin Baoding and supervising secretary Zhao Ruizhang to court with a memorial pleading their case.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，詔諭悔過來朝，且數其五罪：「自平契丹賊、殺劄剌之後，未嘗遣一介赴闕，罪一也。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year an edict urged repentance and attendance at court, enumerating five crimes: "Since pacifying the Khitan bandits and killing Zhala, you have never sent a single envoy to the throne—crime one.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year an edict urged repentance and a visit to court, listing five crimes: "Since the Khitan rebels were pacified and Zhala was killed, you have never sent a single envoy to the throne—crime one.

sentences.zh: 命使齎訓言省諭，輒敢射回，罪二也。

translations.literal: When envoys were sent bearing admonitory words of the court, you dared to shoot them back—crime two.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial envoys came with admonitory instructions, you dared to drive them back by force—crime two.

sentences.zh: 爾等謀害著古歟，乃稱萬奴民戶殺之，罪三也。

translations.literal: You plotted to murder Zhugu'er, yet claimed that commoners of Wannu killed him—crime three.
translations.idiomatic: You plotted to murder Zhugu'er, yet claimed that Wannu's commoners killed him—crime three.

sentences.zh: 命汝進軍，仍令汝弼入朝，爾敢抗拒，竄諸海島，罪四也。

translations.literal: The order was for you to advance your armies, and still for your heir to come to court; you dared to resist and fled to sea islands—crime four.
translations.idiomatic: You were ordered to advance your armies and still to send your heir to court; you resisted and fled to the islands—crime four.

sentences.zh: 汝等民戶不拘集見數，輒敢妄奏，罪五也。

translations.literal: Your registered households, not matching the gathered count, you dared to report falsely—crime five.
translations.idiomatic: Your registered households did not match the muster rolls, yet you dared to report falsely—crime five.

sentences.zh: 」十月，復遣兵攻陷已附西京等處降民，劫洪福源家。

translations.literal: " In the tenth month they again sent troops, storming places where surrendered people of the Western Capital and elsewhere had submitted, and raiding Hong Fuyuan's household.
translations.idiomatic: " In the tenth month they again sent troops, overran communities that had already submitted in the Western Capital region, and plundered Hong Fuyuan's household.

sentences.zh: 六年，福源得請，領其降民遷居東京，賜佩金符。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Fuyuan obtained permission and led his surrendered people to resettle in Dongjing, and was granted a gold tally to wear.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Fuyuan obtained permission to move his surrendered people to Dongjing and was granted a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 七年，命唐古與洪福源領兵征之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Tanggu and Hong Fuyuan were ordered to lead troops in campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Tanggu and Hong Fuyuan were ordered to lead troops against them.

sentences.zh: 九年，拔其龍岡、咸從等十餘城。

translations.literal: In the ninth year they took Longgang, Hyeonjong, and more than ten other cities.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year they captured Longgang, Hyeonjong, and more than ten other cities.

sentences.zh: 十年五月，其國人趙玄習、李元祐等率二千人迎降，命居東京，受洪福源節制，且賜御前銀符，使玄習等佩之，以招未降民戶。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the tenth year the countrymen Zhao Xuanxi, Li Won'yu, and others led two thousand men to surrender; they were ordered to dwell in Dongjing under Hong Fuyuan's command, and imperial silver tallies before the throne were granted for Xuanxi and the others to wear, to summon unsubmitted households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the tenth year Zhao Xuanxi, Li Won'yu, and others led two thousand men to submit; they were settled in Dongjing under Hong Fuyuan's command, given imperial silver tallies to wear, and sent to win over households still holding out.

sentences.zh: 又李君式等十二人來降，待之如玄習焉。

translations.literal: Also Li Gun-seok and twelve others came to surrender and were treated like Xuanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gun-seok and twelve others also submitted and were treated the same way as Xuanxi.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遣其將軍金寶鼎、御史宋彥琦等奉表入朝。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month they sent their general Jin Baoding, censor Song Yeon-gi, and others presenting a memorial to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month they sent their general Jin Baoding, censor Song Yeon-gi, and others to court with a memorial.

sentences.zh: 十一年五月，詔徵入朝，以母喪辭。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eleventh year an edict summoned him to court; he declined on grounds of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eleventh year an edict summoned him to court, but he declined on account of his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 六月，乃遣其禮賓卿盧演、禮賓少卿金謙充進奉使、副，奉表入朝。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he then sent his Master of Guests Lu Yeon, Vice Master of Guests Jin Qian as chief tributary envoy and deputy, presenting a memorial to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he sent his Master of Guests Lu Yeon and Vice Master of Guests Jin Qian as chief tributary envoy and deputy with a memorial to court.

sentences.zh: 十月，有旨諭，徵其親朝於明年。

translations.literal: In the tenth month an order was issued that he should come in person the following year.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month an order was issued requiring him to come to court in person the following year.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遣其新安公王佺與寶鼎、彥琦等百四十八人奉表入貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he sent his Duke of Xin'an Wang Yeon, Baoding, Yeon-gi, and one hundred forty-eight others presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he sent the Duke of Xin'an Wang Yeon, Jin Baoding, Song Yeon-gi, and one hundred forty-eight others to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 十二年三月，又遣其右諫議大夫趙修、閤門祗候金成寶等奉表入貢。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twelfth year he again sent his Right Remonstrator Zhao Su, Gate Attendant Jin Seongbo, and others presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twelfth year he again sent his Right Remonstrator Zhao Su, Gate Attendant Jin Seongbo, and others with tribute.

sentences.zh: 五月，復下詔諭之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month an edict was again issued instructing them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month another edict was issued to instruct them.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遣其禮賓少卿宋彥琦、侍御史權韙充行李使入貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he sent Vice Master of Guests Song Yeon-gi and attendant censor Gwon Hwi as baggage envoys presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he sent Vice Master of Guests Song Yeon-gi and attendant censor Gwon Hwi as baggage envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 是歲，攻拔昌、朔等州。

translations.literal: That year they stormed and took Chang, Seo, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: That year they captured the prefectures of Chang, Seo, and others.

sentences.zh: 十三年秋，以族子綧為己子入質。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the thirteenth year he sent his clansman Son, presented as his own son, to serve as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the thirteenth year he sent his clansman Son, presented as his own son, to court as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 當定宗、憲宗之世，歲貢不入，故自定宗二年至憲宗八年，凡四命將征之，凡拔其城十有四。

translations.literal: During the reigns of Dingzong and Xianzong annual tribute was not submitted; therefore from the second year of Dingzong to the eighth year of Xianzong, commanders were sent to campaign four times in all, taking fourteen of their cities.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dingzong and Xianzong annual tribute ceased, so from Dingzong's second year to Xianzong's eighth year generals were sent on campaign four times and fourteen of their cities were taken.

sentences.zh: 憲宗末，遣其世子倎入朝。

translations.literal: At the end of Xianzong's reign he sent his heir Prince Che to court.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Xianzong's reign he sent his heir, Prince Che, to court.

sentences.zh: 我太祖皇帝肇開大業，聖聖相承，代有鴻勳，芟夷群雄，奄有四海，未嘗專嗜殺也。

translations.literal: Our Taizu Emperor inaugurated the great enterprise; sagely succession followed, each generation achieving glorious merit, cutting down rival heroes and embracing all within the Four Seas, yet never indulging slaughter for its own sake.
translations.idiomatic: Our Taizu Emperor founded the great enterprise; sage succeeded sage, each generation winning splendid merit, cutting down rival powers and embracing all within the Four Seas, yet never delighting in slaughter for its own sake.

sentences.zh: 凡屬國列侯，分茅錫土，傳祚子孫者，不啻萬里，孰非向之勍敵哉。

translations.literal: For feudatory states and enfeoffed lords who received fiefs and passed their domains to their sons, there were no fewer than ten thousand li of them—were they not all once formidable foes?
translations.idiomatic: The vassal states and enfeoffed lords who received fiefs and passed their domains to their sons stretch more than ten thousand li—were they not all once formidable foes?

sentences.zh: 觀乎此，則祖宗之法不待言而章章矣。

translations.literal: Viewed thus, the ancestral law needs no words spoken—it is manifest indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, the ancestral way needs no words to make it clear.

sentences.zh: 今也，普天之下未臣服者，惟爾國與宋耳。

translations.literal: Now, under the whole heaven the only ones not yet submitted are your country and Song.
translations.idiomatic: Now, under all heaven only your country and Song have not yet submitted.

sentences.zh: 宋所恃者長江，而長江失險；

translations.literal: What Song relied on was the Yangtze, but the Yangtze has lost its strategic depth;
translations.idiomatic: Song relied on the Yangtze, but the Yangtze no longer protects it;

sentences.zh: 所藉者川、廣，而川、廣不支。

translations.literal: what it counted on were Sichuan and Guangdong, yet Sichuan and Guangdong cannot sustain it.
translations.idiomatic: it counted on Sichuan and Guangdong, yet Sichuan and Guangdong can no longer sustain it.

sentences.zh: 邊戍自徹其藩籬，大軍已駐乎心腹，鼎魚幕燕，亡在旦夕。

translations.literal: Border garrisons have already pulled away their defenses, and great armies already stand at their heartland; like fish in a cauldron or swallows under a roof, their destruction is imminent.
translations.idiomatic: Its border defenses have already fallen away, and great armies already stand in its heartland; like fish in a cauldron or swallows under a roof, its end is near.

sentences.zh: 爾初以世子奉幣納款，束身歸朝，含哀請命，良可矜憫，故遣歸國，完復舊疆，安爾田疇，保爾室家，弘好生之大德，捐宿構之細故也。

translations.literal: You first sent your heir with gifts to submit, binding yourself to return to court in mourning and begging for mercy—truly pitiable; therefore you were sent home, your old domain restored, your fields secured, your households protected, extending the great virtue of cherishing life and discarding old petty grievances.
translations.idiomatic: You first sent your heir with gifts to submit, came yourself in mourning garb to beg for mercy—a case truly deserving pity; therefore you were sent home, your old domain restored, your fields secured, your households protected, extending the great virtue of cherishing life and setting aside old grievances.

sentences.zh: 用是已嘗戒敕邊將，斂兵待命，東方既定，則將迴戈於錢塘。

translations.literal: For this the border generals were already enjoined to hold their armies in readiness; once the east was settled, they would wheel westward toward Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the border generals were already ordered to hold their armies in readiness; once the east was settled they would turn their spears toward Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 迨餘半載，乃知爾國內亂渝盟，邊將復請戒嚴，此何故也？

translations.literal: After half a year it became known that your country had internal disorder and violated the covenant, and the border generals again requested martial alert—what is the cause of this?
translations.idiomatic: After half a year it became clear that your country had fallen into internal disorder and broken the covenant, and the border generals again asked for martial alert—what is the reason for this?

sentences.zh: 以謂果內亂耶，權臣何不自立，而立世孫？

translations.literal: If it was truly internal disorder, why did the powerful minister not set himself up as ruler but instead installed the heir's descendant?
translations.idiomatic: If there was truly internal disorder, why did the powerful minister not seize the throne himself but instead set up the heir's descendant?

sentences.zh: 以謂傳聞之誤耶，世子何不之國而盤桓於境上也？

translations.literal: If it was mistaken rumor, why did the heir not enter the country but linger on the frontier?
translations.idiomatic: If it was mere rumor, why did the heir not enter the country but linger on the border?

sentences.zh: 豈以世子之歸愆期，而左右自相猜疑，私憂過計而然耶？

translations.literal: Could it be that because the heir's return was overdue, those around him grew suspicious through private anxiety and excessive caution?
translations.idiomatic: Could it be that because the heir's return was overdue, those around him grew suspicious through private anxiety and excessive caution?

sentences.zh: 重念島嶼殘民，久罹塗炭，窮兵極討，殆非本心。

translations.literal: Taking again thought for the remnant people on the islands who have long suffered ruin, exhausting war is hardly our true intent.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking again of the remnant people on the islands who have long suffered ruin, to press war to the limit is hardly our true intent.

sentences.zh: 且御失其道，則天下狙詐咸作敵；

translations.literal: When the ruler loses the Way, then deceit and treachery throughout the realm all become enemies;
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler loses the Way, deceit and treachery throughout the realm all become enemies;

sentences.zh: 推赤心置人腹中，則反側之輩自安矣。

translations.literal: but when one lays an open heart in another's breast, those of contrary intent will be at peace of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: but when one lays an open heart in another's breast, those of contrary intent will be at peace of themselves.

sentences.zh: 悠悠之言，又何足校。

translations.literal: Idle talk is not worth contesting.
translations.idiomatic: Idle rumors are not worth answering.

sentences.zh: 申命邊閫，斷自予衷，無以逋逃間執政，無以飛語亂定盟。

translations.literal: Orders are reaffirmed to the border: my mind is decided—do not let fugitives come between the government, do not let flying rumors disorder the settled covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Orders are reaffirmed to the border command: my mind is decided—do not let fugitives come between the government, and do not let flying rumors disturb the settled covenant.

sentences.zh: 惟事推誠，一切勿問。

translations.literal: Only push sincerity in affairs; question nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: Only act with sincerity in all matters; question nothing else.

sentences.zh: 宜施曠蕩之恩，一新遐邇之化。

translations.literal: Broad pardoning grace should be applied, renewing transformation far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Broad pardoning grace should be applied, renewing transformation far and near.

sentences.zh: 自尚書金仁雋以次，中外枝黨、官吏、軍民，聖旨到日已前，或有首謀內亂，旅拒王師，已降附而還叛，因仇讎而擅殺，無所歸而背主亡命，不得已而隨衆脅從，應據國人但曾犯法，罪無輕重咸赦除之。

translations.literal: From Minister Jin In-gyun downward, whether central or local faction, officials, soldiers, or civilians, before the day this sacred edict arrives, whoever among the people of the country once violated the law—whether chief instigators of internal disorder, resisting the royal army, having submitted and then rebelled again, killing through private enmity, having nowhere to turn and fleeing from their lord, or forced to follow the crowd against their will—all crimes light or heavy are pardoned and erased.
translations.idiomatic: From Minister Jin In-gyun downward, whether central or local faction, officials, soldiers, or civilians, before the day this sacred edict arrives—whether chief instigators of internal disorder, resisting the royal army, having submitted and then rebelled again, killing through private enmity, having nowhere to turn and fleeing from their lord, or forced to follow the crowd against their will—all subjects of the country who once violated the law, whatever the gravity of the crime, are pardoned and absolved.

sentences.zh: 世子其趣裝命駕，歸國知政，解仇釋憾，布德施恩。

translations.literal: The heir should pack and set out at once, return to govern his state, resolve hatreds and release grievances, spread virtue and bestow grace.
translations.idiomatic: Heir, make ready and set out at once; return to govern your state, resolve hatreds and release grievances, spread virtue and bestow grace.

sentences.zh: 緬惟瘡痍之民，正在撫綏之日，出彼滄溟，宅於平壤。

translations.literal: Pondering the wounded people, this is precisely the time for soothing governance; lead them from the eastern sea to dwell in Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Think of the wounded people—this is precisely the time to soothe them; lead them from the eastern sea to dwell in Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 賣刀劍而買牛犢，捨干戈而操耒耜，凡可援濟，毋憚勤勞。

translations.literal: Sell swords for oxen, lay aside weapons for ploughs—all aid that can be offered, spare no labor.
translations.idiomatic: Sell swords to buy oxen, lay aside weapons for ploughs; in every way that aid can be given, spare no labor.

sentences.zh: 苟富庶之有徵，冀禮義之可復，亟正疆界，以定民心，我師不復踰限矣。

translations.literal: If prosperity shows its signs, then rites and righteousness may be restored; swiftly rectify boundaries to settle the people's hearts, and our armies will not again cross the line.
translations.idiomatic: If prosperity shows its signs, then rites and righteousness may be restored; swiftly rectify your boundaries to settle the people's hearts, and our armies will not again cross the line.

sentences.zh: 大號一出，朕不食言。

translations.literal: Once this great proclamation issues, I will not eat my words.
translations.idiomatic: Once this great proclamation issues, I will not go back on my word.

sentences.zh: 復有敢踵亂犯上者，非干爾主，乃亂我典刑，國有常憲，人得誅之。

translations.literal: If anyone dares again to foment rebellion and offend superiors, it will not implicate your lord but will disturb our statutes; the state has constant punishments, and anyone may execute such offenders.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone dares again to foment rebellion and offend superiors, it will not implicate your lord but will disturb our statutes; the state has fixed punishments, and anyone may execute such offenders.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 世子其王矣，往欽哉，恭承丕訓，永為東藩，以揚我休命。

translations.literal: Heir, take the kingship; go—revere this charge, continue the great instruction, and forever be the eastern feudatory, to manifest our gracious mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Heir, take the kingship; go—revere this charge, continue the great instruction, and forever be the eastern feudatory, to manifest our gracious mandate.

sentences.zh: 四月，復降旨諭倎曰：「朕祗若天命，獲承祖宗休烈，仰惟覆燾，一視同仁，無遐邇小大之間也。

translations.literal: In the fourth month an edict was again issued to Che, saying: "I reverently follow Heaven's mandate, inheriting my ancestors' glorious enterprise; looking up I cover and nurture all alike, making no distinction between far and near, small and great.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month another edict was issued to Che, saying, "I reverently follow Heaven's mandate and inherit my ancestors' glorious enterprise; looking up I cover and nurture all alike, making no distinction between far and near, small and great.

sentences.zh: 以爾歸款，既冊為王還國，今得爾與邊將之書，因知其上下之情，朕甚憫焉。

translations.literal: Because you submitted and were enfeoffed as king and returned to your country, now receiving your letters and those of the border generals, I know the sentiments above and below—I pity you greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Because you submitted and were enfeoffed as king and sent home, I have now received your letters and those of the border generals and understand the feelings of your court; I pity you deeply.

sentences.zh: 」倎求出水就陸，免軍馬侵擾，還被虜及逃民，皆從之。

translations.literal: " Che requested to leave the water and come onto land, freedom from army and horse harassment, and return of captives and fugitive subjects—all were granted.
translations.idiomatic: " Che asked to leave the islands for the mainland, to be spared harassment by troops and horses, and to have captives and fugitive subjects returned—all were granted.

sentences.zh: 詔班師，乃赦其境內。

translations.literal: An edict ordered withdrawal of troops, and then pardon was granted within their territory.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the armies to withdraw, and a general pardon was then proclaimed within their territory.

sentences.zh: 六月，倎遣其子永安公僖、判司宰事韓即入賀即位，以國王封冊、王印及虎符賜之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Che sent his son the Duke of Yong'an Wang Xi and Chief of the Office of Royal Granaries Han Je to congratulate the enthronement; the king's enfeoffment patent, royal seal, and tiger tally were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Che sent his son, the Duke of Yong'an Wang Xi, and the chief of the Office of Royal Granaries Han Je to congratulate the enthronement; the king's patent of enfeoffment, royal seal, and tiger tally were bestowed on him.

sentences.zh: 是月，又下詔撫諭之。

translations.literal: That month another edict was issued to comfort and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: That month another edict was issued to comfort and instruct them.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year envoys were sent with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year envoys were sent with tribute.

sentences.zh: 四月，倎入朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Che came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Che came to court in person.

sentences.zh: 六月，倎更名禃，遣其世子愖奉表以聞。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Che changed his name to Chung, and sent his heir Prince Sim to present a memorial informing the court.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Che changed his name to Chung and sent his heir Prince Sim with a memorial to inform the court.

sentences.zh: 八月，賜禃玉帶一，遣侍衛將軍孛里察、禮部郎中高逸民護愖還國。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Chung was granted one jade belt; Palace Guard general Boricha and Ministry of Rites secretary Gao Yimin escorted Sim back.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Chung was granted a jade belt, and Palace Guard general Boricha and Ministry of Rites secretary Gao Yimin escorted Sim home.

sentences.zh: 九月，禃遣其侍御史張鎰奉表入謝。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Chung sent his attendant censor Jang Eui with a memorial to thank the court.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Chung sent his attendant censor Jang Eui to court with a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 十月，帝遣阿的迷失、焦天翼持詔，諭以開榷場事。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Emperor sent Adishimu and Jiao Tianyi with an edict instructing them on establishing controlled markets.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Emperor sent Adishimu and Jiao Tianyi with an edict instructing them on opening controlled markets.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，罷互市。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year mutual markets were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year the mutual markets were abolished.

sentences.zh: 諸王塔察兒請置鐵冶，從之。

translations.literal: Prince Tachar requested establishment of ironworks—this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tachar requested the establishment of ironworks, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 請立互市，不從。

translations.literal: A request to establish mutual markets was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: A request to re-establish mutual markets was refused.

sentences.zh: 賜禃曆，後歲以為常，禃遣使入謝，優詔荅之。

translations.literal: Chung was granted the imperial calendar; in later years this became regular; Chung sent envoys to thank, and a favorable edict replied.
translations.idiomatic: Chung was granted the imperial calendar, and in later years this became the regular practice; Chung sent envoys to thank the court, and a gracious edict replied.

sentences.zh: 四月，禃遣其左諫議大夫朴倫、郎將辛洪成等奉表入朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Chung sent his Left Remonstrator Bak Yun, commandant Sin Hongseong, and others presenting a memorial to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Chung sent his Left Remonstrator Bak Yun, commandant Sin Hongseong, and others to court with a memorial.

sentences.zh: 六月，遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth month envoys were sent with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month envoys were sent with tribute.

sentences.zh: 八月，朴倫等還，賜西錦三段、間金熟綾六段。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Bak Yun and the others returned; they were granted three lengths of western brocade and six lengths of gold-threaded figured silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Bak Yun and the others returned and were granted three lengths of western brocade and six lengths of gold-threaded figured silk.

sentences.zh: 十月，詔諭禃籍編民，出師旅，輸糧餉，助軍儲。

translations.literal: In the tenth month an edict instructed Chung to register the people, furnish troops, supply grain, and assist military stores.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month an edict instructed Chung to register the people, furnish troops, supply grain rations, and assist military stores.

sentences.zh: 是月，禃遣使入貢。

translations.literal: That month Chung sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That month Chung sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，以禃不荅詔書，詰其使者。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, because Chung had not replied to the edict, his envoys were questioned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year, because Chung had not replied to the edict, his envoys were questioned.

sentences.zh: 禃表乞俟民生稍集，然後惟命。

translations.literal: Chung submitted a memorial asking to wait until the people's livelihood had somewhat recovered, and then he would obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: Chung submitted a memorial asking to wait until the people's livelihood had somewhat recovered before obeying orders.

sentences.zh: 帝以其辭意懇實，允之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, finding his words earnest and sincere, granted this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, finding his words earnest and sincere, granted the request.

sentences.zh: 朝貢物數，亦命稱其力焉。

translations.literal: The quantities of tribute items were also ordered to match their capacity.
translations.idiomatic: The quantities of tribute items were also ordered to match their capacity.

sentences.zh: 自三月至于六月，禃凡三遣使入貢，賜禃羊五百。

translations.literal: From the third month to the sixth, Chung sent envoys with tribute three times in all; Chung was granted five hundred sheep.
translations.idiomatic: From the third month to the sixth Chung sent tribute missions three times, and was granted five hundred sheep.

sentences.zh: 十一月，禃以免置驛籍民等事，遣其翰林學士韓就奉表入謝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on account of exemption from post-station service and registered households and other matters, Chung sent his Hanlin academician Han Je with a memorial to thank the court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Chung sent his Hanlin academician Han Je to court with a memorial of thanks for exemptions regarding post-stations and registered households.

sentences.zh: 五年正月丁丑朔，禃遣使奉表入賀，諭還使，令禃親朝京師。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month, dingchou, of the fifth year, Chung sent envoys with a memorial to congratulate the New Year; the returning envoys were instructed that Chung should come in person to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the fifth year Chung sent envoys with a congratulatory memorial; the returning envoys were told that Chung must come to the capital in person.

sentences.zh: 四月，以西北諸王率衆款附，擬今歲朝王公群牧于上都，又遣必闍赤古乙獨徵禃入朝，修世見之禮。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, because the princes of the northwest led their followers in submission, it was planned that this year the kings, dukes, and tribal chiefs would attend court at Shangdu; Bicheke Guyidu was again sent to summon Chung to court to perform the rite of audience by generations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, because the northwestern princes led their followers in submission, it was planned that kings, dukes, and tribal chiefs would attend court at Shangdu that year; Bicheke Guyidu was again sent to summon Chung to perform the rite of audience by generations.

sentences.zh: 五月，禃遣其借國子祭酒張鎰從古乙獨入見，六月乃親朝。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Chung sent his acting Director of the National University Jang Eui to follow Guyidu in audience; in the sixth month he came to court in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Chung sent his acting Director of the National University Jang Eui to follow Guyidu to audience; in the sixth month he came to court in person.

sentences.zh: 九月，帝以改中統五年為至元元年，遣郎中路得成持赦令，與禃郎將康允紹頒其國。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, because the fifth year of Zhongtong was changed to the first year of Zhiyuan, Langzhong Lu Decheng was sent bearing an amnesty, and with Chung's commandant Kang Yunso it was promulgated in their country.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, because the fifth year of Zhongtong was changed to the first year of Zhiyuan, Langzhong Lu Decheng was sent with an amnesty, which he promulgated in Goryeo together with Chung's commandant Kang Yunso.

sentences.zh: 十月，禃入朝。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Chung came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Chung came to court.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遣禃還國。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Chung was sent back to his country.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Chung was sent back to his country.

sentences.zh: 是年春，禃遣使入貢。

translations.literal: That spring Chung sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Chung sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 自是終世祖三十一年，其國入貢者凡三十有六。

translations.literal: From then until the end of Shizu's thirty-one years, their country sent tribute thirty-six times in all.
translations.idiomatic: From then until the end of Kublai's thirty-one-year reign, Goryeo sent tribute thirty-six times in all.

sentences.zh: 至元三年二月，立瀋州，以處高麗降民。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Zhiyuan Shen Prefecture was established to settle surrendered Goryeo people.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Zhiyuan 3 Shen Prefecture was established to settle surrendered Goryeo subjects.

sentences.zh: 帝欲通好日本，以高麗與日本鄰國，可為鄉導，八月，遣國信使兵部侍郎黑的、禮部侍郎殷弘、計議官伯德孝先等使日本，先至高麗諭旨。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to open relations with Japan; because Goryeo was a neighboring country of Japan and could serve as guide, in the eighth month he sent credentialed envoys Vice Minister of War Hei Di, Vice Minister of Rites Yin Hong, planning officer Bode Xiaoxian, and others to Japan, first reaching Goryeo to convey the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to open relations with Japan; because Goryeo bordered Japan and could serve as guide, in the eighth month he sent credentialed envoys Vice Minister of War Hei Di, Vice Minister of Rites Yin Hong, and planning officer Bode Xiaoxian to Japan, first reaching Goryeo to convey the imperial intent.

sentences.zh: 十二月，禃遣其樞密院副使宋君斐、借禮部侍郎金贊等導詔使黑的、殷弘等往日本，不至而還。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Chung sent his privy council vice commissioner Song Gunbi, acting Vice Minister of Rites Kim Chan, and others to guide the imperial envoys Hei Di, Yin Hong, and the rest to Japan; they did not reach Japan and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Chung sent his privy council vice commissioner Song Gunbi, acting Vice Minister of Rites Kim Chan, and others to guide the imperial envoys Hei Di and Yin Hong to Japan; they did not reach Japan and returned.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，禃遣君斐等奉表從黑的等入朝。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year Chung sent Gunbi and others with a memorial, following Hei Di and the rest to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year Chung sent Gunbi and others to court with a memorial, following Hei Di and the rest.

sentences.zh: 六月，帝以禃飾辭，令去使徒還，復遣黑的與君斐等以詔諭禃，委以日本事，以必得其要領為期。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Emperor, because Chung's words were evasive, ordered the departing envoys to return empty-handed; Hei Di and Gunbi were again sent with an edict to instruct Chung, entrusting him with Japanese affairs on the condition that the essential points must be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Emperor, finding Chung's words evasive, ordered the departing envoys to return empty-handed; Hei Di and Gunbi were again sent with an edict instructing Chung and entrusting him with Japanese affairs, on condition that the essential points must be obtained.

sentences.zh: 九月，禃遣其起居舍人潘阜、書狀官李挺充國信使，持書詣日本。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Chung sent his chamberlain for attendance Pan Fu and document officer Li Ting as credentialed envoys bearing a letter to Japan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Chung sent his chamberlain for attendance Pan Fu and document officer Li Ting as credentialed envoys with a letter to Japan.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，禃遣其弟淐入朝。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year Chung sent his younger brother Cheo to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year Chung sent his younger brother Cheo to court.

sentences.zh: 帝以禃見欺於淐，面數其事切責之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Chung had been deceived by Cheo, recounted the matter to his face and sternly rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, because Chung had been deceived by Cheo, recounted the matter to his face and sternly rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 特遣北京路緫管兼大定府尹于也孫脫、禮部郎中孟甲持詔諭禃，其略曰：「向請撤兵，則已撤之矣。

translations.literal: He specially sent Beiping Circuit administrator and concurrent Dading prefect Yexiesuntuo and Ministry of Rites director Meng Jia with an edict to instruct Chung; the gist was: "When you asked for withdrawal of troops, they were withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: He specially sent Beiping Circuit administrator and concurrent Dading prefect Yexiesuntuo and Ministry of Rites director Meng Jia with an edict to instruct Chung, saying in substance: "When you asked for withdrawal of troops, they were withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 三年當去水就陸，而前言無徵也。

translations.literal: In the third year you were to leave the water and come onto land, yet your earlier words have not been verified.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year you were to leave the islands for the mainland, yet your earlier promises have not been fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 又太祖法制，凡內屬之國，納質、助軍、輸糧、設驛、編戶籍、置長官，已嘗明諭之，而稽延至今，終無成言。

translations.literal: Moreover, by Taizu's institutions, for all inner-subject states: sending hostages, assisting armies, supplying grain, establishing post stations, compiling household registers, and installing chief officials—all this was clearly instructed, yet you have delayed until today and in the end have given no settled reply.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, by Taizu's institutions all inner-subject states must send hostages, assist armies, supply grain, establish post stations, compile household registers, and install chief officials—all this was clearly instructed, yet you have delayed until today without a settled reply.

sentences.zh: 在太宗時，王綧等已入質，驛傳亦粗立，餘率未奉行。

translations.literal: Under Taizong, Wang Son and others had already come as hostages, and post relays were roughly established; the rest for the most part have not been carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong, Wang Son and others had already come as hostages, and post relays were roughly established; the rest for the most part have not been carried out.

sentences.zh: 今將問罪於宋，其所助士卒舟艦幾何？

translations.literal: Now we are about to call Song to account—how many troops and ships will you supply?
translations.idiomatic: Now we are about to call Song to account—how many troops and ships will you supply?

sentences.zh: 輸糧則就為儲積，至若設官及戶版事，其意謂何？

translations.literal: Grain supplies should be made ready as stores; as for installing officials and household registers, what is your intent?
translations.idiomatic: Grain should be made ready as stores; as for installing officials and household registers, what is your intent?

sentences.zh: 故以問之。

translations.literal: Therefore I ask these things.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I ask these things.

sentences.zh: 」三月，于也孫脫等至其國。

translations.literal: " In the third month Yexiesuntuo and the others reached their country.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third month Yexiesuntuo and the others reached Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 四月，禃遣其門下侍郎李藏用奉表與也孫脫等入朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Chung sent his Secretariat vice minister Li Cangyong with a memorial, following Yexiesuntuo and the others to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Chung sent his Secretariat vice minister Li Cangyong to court with a memorial, following Yexiesuntuo and the others.

sentences.zh: 五月，帝敕藏用曰：「往諭爾主，速以軍數實奏，將遣人督之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Emperor charged Cangyong: "Go instruct your lord to report the true military numbers at once; I shall send men to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Emperor charged Cangyong: "Go tell your lord to report the true military numbers at once; I shall send men to supervise.

sentences.zh: 今出軍，爾等必疑將出何地，或欲南宋，或欲日本，爾主當造舟一千艘，能涉大海可載四千石者。

translations.literal: Now that troops are to be sent out, you will surely wonder where they are bound—whether against Southern Song or against Japan; your lord must build one thousand ships able to cross the great sea and carry four thousand piculs each.
translations.idiomatic: Now that troops are to be sent out, you will surely wonder where they are bound—whether against Southern Song or Japan; your lord must build one thousand ships able to cross the open sea and carry four thousand piculs each.

sentences.zh: 」藏用曰：「舟艦之事即當應命，但人民殘少，恐不及期。

translations.literal: " Cangyong said: "The matter of ships will be obeyed at once, but the people are few and devastated; I fear we cannot meet the deadline.
translations.idiomatic: " Cangyong said, "The ships will be provided at once, but our people are few and devastated; I fear we cannot meet the deadline.

sentences.zh: 往者臣國有軍四萬，三十餘年間死於兵疫，今止有牌子頭、五十戶、百戶、千戶之類虛名，而無軍卒。

translations.literal: Formerly my country had forty thousand troops; over more than thirty years they died in war and pestilence; now there remain only empty titles such as platoon head, fifty-household chief, hundred-household chief, and thousand-household chief, but no soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly our country had forty thousand troops; over more than thirty years they perished in war and pestilence; now there remain only empty titles such as platoon head and fifty-, hundred-, and thousand-household chiefs, but no soldiers.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「死者有之，生者亦有之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Some have died, but some have also been born.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "Some have died, but some have also been born.

sentences.zh: 」藏用曰：「賴聖德，自撤兵以來，有生長者僅十歲耳。

translations.literal: " Cangyong said: "Thanks to your sacred virtue, since the withdrawal of troops those who have grown up are only about ten years old.
translations.idiomatic: " Cangyong said, "Thanks to your sacred virtue, since the withdrawal of troops those who have grown to maturity are only about ten years old.

sentences.zh: 」帝又曰：「自爾來者言，海中之事，於宋得便風可三日而至，日本則朝發而夕至。

translations.literal: " The Emperor also said: "According to what your envoys have said, at sea with a fair wind one can reach Song in three days, and Japan can be reached setting out in the morning and arriving in the evening.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor also said, "According to what your envoys have said, with a fair wind one can reach Song in three days at sea, and Japan can be reached setting out in the morning and arriving in the evening.

sentences.zh: 舟中載米，海中捕魚而食之，則豈不可行乎？

translations.literal: If ships carry grain and fish are caught at sea for food, how can it not be feasible?
translations.idiomatic: If ships carry grain and fish are caught at sea for food, how can it not be feasible?

sentences.zh: 」又敕藏用曰：「歸可以此言諭爾主。」

translations.literal: " He again charged Cangyong: "On your return you may use these words to instruct your lord."
translations.idiomatic: " He again charged Cangyong: "On your return you may convey these words to your lord."

sentences.zh: 七月，詔都統領脫朶兒、武德將軍統領王國昌、武略將軍副統領劉傑等使其國，與其來朝者大將軍崔東秀偕行。

translations.literal: In the seventh month an edict ordered supreme commander Tuoduo'er, Martial Virtue general commander Wang Guochang, Martial Strategy general vice commander Liu Jie, and others to their country, traveling with their court visitor, great general Choe Dongsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month an edict ordered supreme commander Tuoduo'er, Martial Virtue general commander Wang Guochang, Martial Strategy general vice commander Liu Jie, and others to Goryeo, traveling with the great general Choe Dongsu who had come to court.

sentences.zh: 八月，至其國，禃出昇天府迎之，蓋諭以閱軍造船也。

translations.literal: In the eighth month they reached their country; Chung came out from Shengtian Prefecture to welcome them—this was to instruct them on inspecting troops and building ships.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month they reached Goryeo; Chung came out from Shengtian Prefecture to welcome them, for they had come to inspect troops and oversee shipbuilding.

sentences.zh: 九月，以禃表奏潘阜等奉使無功而還，復遣黑的等使日本，詔禃遣重臣導送。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, because Chung's memorial reported that Pan Fu and the others had returned from their mission without success, Hei Di and others were again sent to Japan; an edict ordered Chung to send high ministers to guide and escort them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, because Chung reported that Pan Fu's mission had returned without success, Hei Di and others were again sent to Japan, and Chung was ordered to send high ministers to guide and escort them.

sentences.zh: 十二月，禃遣其知門下省事申思佺、禮部侍郎陳井、起居舍人潘阜等從國信使黑的等赴日本，借禮部侍郎張鎰奉表從脫朶兒入朝。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Chung sent his Secretariat affairs officer Sin Sijeon, Vice Minister of Rites Chen Jing, chamberlain for attendance Pan Fu, and others to follow the credentialed envoys Hei Di and the rest to Japan; acting Vice Minister of Rites Jang Eui presented a memorial, following Tuoduo'er to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Chung sent his Secretariat affairs officer Sin Sijeon, Vice Minister of Rites Chen Jing, chamberlain Pan Fu, and others to accompany the credentialed envoys Hei Di to Japan; acting Vice Minister of Rites Jang Eui went to court with a memorial, following Tuoduo'er.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，禃遣其大將軍康允紹奉表奏誅權臣金俊等。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year Chung sent his great general Kang Yunso with a memorial reporting the execution of the powerful minister Kim Jun and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year Chung sent his great general Kang Yunso with a memorial reporting the execution of the powerful minister Kim Jun and others.

sentences.zh: 三月，禃復遣申思佺奉表從黑的入朝。

translations.literal: In the third month Chung again sent Sin Sijeon with a memorial, following Hei Di to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Chung again sent Sin Sijeon to court with a memorial, following Hei Di.

sentences.zh: 六月，禃遣其世子愖入朝。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Chung sent his heir Prince Sim to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Chung sent his heir Prince Sim to court.

sentences.zh: 賜禃玉帶一，愖金五十兩，從官銀幣有差。

translations.literal: Chung was granted one jade belt; Sim was granted fifty taels of gold; accompanying officials received silver coins in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Chung was granted a jade belt; Sim was granted fifty taels of gold; accompanying officials received silver in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 七月，帝遣明威將軍都統領脫朶兒、武德將軍統領王國昌、武略將軍副統領劉傑相視耽羅等處道路，詔禃選官引達，以人言耽羅海道往南宋、日本甚易故也。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Emperor sent Bright Authority general supreme commander Tuoduo'er, Martial Virtue general commander Wang Guochang, and Martial Strategy general vice commander Liu Jie to inspect the roads at Tamna and elsewhere; an edict ordered Chung to select officials to guide them, because people said the Tamna sea route to Southern Song and Japan was very easy.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Emperor sent Tuoduo'er, Wang Guochang, and Liu Jie to inspect the roads at Tamna and elsewhere; Chung was ordered to select officials to guide them, because people said the Tamna sea route to Southern Song and Japan was very easy.

sentences.zh: 八月，世子愖至朝，奏本國臣下擅廢禃立其弟安慶公淐事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the heir Prince Sim reached court and reported that subjects of his country had on their own authority deposed Chung and set up his younger brother the Duke of Anqing Cheo.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Prince Sim reached court and reported that his country's subjects had on their own authority deposed Chung and installed his younger brother, the Duke of Anqing Cheo.

sentences.zh: 詔遣使臣斡朶思不花、李諤等至其國詳問之。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched envoys Woduosibuhua, Li E, and others to their country to investigate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched envoys Woduosibuhua, Li E, and others to Goryeo to investigate in detail.

sentences.zh: 九月，其樞密院副使金方慶奉表從斡朶思不花等入朝。

translations.literal: In the ninth month their privy council vice commissioner Kim Banggyeong presented a memorial, following Woduosibuhua and the others to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month their privy council vice commissioner Kim Banggyeong came to court with a memorial, following Woduosibuhua and the others.

sentences.zh: 樞密院御史臺奏，世子愖言：「朝廷若出征，能辦軍三千，備糧五月，如官軍入境，臣宜同往，庶不驚擾。

translations.literal: The Privy Council and Censorate reported that the heir Prince Sim said: "If the court campaigns, I can furnish three thousand troops and provisions for five months; if the official army enters our territory, I ought to go with them, so that there may be no alarm or disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: The Privy Council and Censorate reported that Prince Sim said, "If the court campaigns, I can furnish three thousand troops and five months' provisions; if the imperial army enters our territory, I ought to go with them so that the people will not be alarmed.

sentences.zh: 」帝然之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 詔授世子禃特進、上柱國，敕愖率兵三千赴其國難。

translations.literal: An edict granted the heir Chung the special advancement and designation Superior Pillar of State; Sim was charged to lead three thousand troops to relieve the crisis in his country.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted Chung the special advancement and designation Superior Pillar of State; Sim was ordered to lead three thousand troops to relieve the crisis in his country.

sentences.zh: 命抄不花往征其國，以病不果行，詔遣蒙哥都代之。

translations.literal: Chaobuhua was ordered to campaign against their country; because of illness he did not go, and an edict sent Monggedu in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Chaobuhua was ordered to campaign against Goryeo; because of illness he did not go, and Monggedu was sent in his place.

sentences.zh: 十月，帝以禃、淐廢置乃林衍所為，遣中憲大夫兵部侍郎黑的、淄萊路緫管府判官徐世雄詔禃、淐、衍等以十二月同詣闕下，面陳情實，聽其是非。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Emperor, because the deposition of Chung and Cheo was the work of Im Yon, sent Central Integrity grandee Vice Minister of War Hei Di and Zilai Circuit administration vice commissioner Xu Shixiong with an edict that Chung, Cheo, Yon, and the others should come together to the throne in the twelfth month, state the facts in person, and let right and wrong be heard.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Emperor, holding that the deposition of Chung and Cheo was the work of Im Yon, sent Vice Minister of War Hei Di and Zilai Circuit vice commissioner Xu Shixiong with an edict ordering Chung, Cheo, Yon, and the others to come to court together in the twelfth month and state the facts in person so that right and wrong might be determined.

sentences.zh: 又遣國王頭輦哥等率兵壓境，如踰期不至，即當窮治首惡，進兵勦戮。

translations.literal: The king Tounaige and others were again sent leading troops to press the border; if they did not arrive by the deadline, the chief culprits would be pursued to the end and troops would advance to exterminate them.
translations.idiomatic: Tounaige and others were again sent leading troops to the border; if they did not arrive by the deadline, the chief culprits would be pursued to the end and troops would advance to exterminate them.

sentences.zh: 命趙璧行中書省于東京，仍詔諭高麗國軍民。

translations.literal: Zhao Bi was ordered to conduct the Secretariat at Dongjing, and an edict was again issued instructing the soldiers and people of Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bi was ordered to conduct the Secretariat at Dongjing, and an edict was again issued to the soldiers and people of Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 十一月，高麗都統領崔坦等以林衍作亂，挈西京五十餘城入附。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the Goryeo supreme commander Choe Tan and others, because Im Yon had raised rebellion, brought more than fifty cities of the Western Capital to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Goryeo supreme commander Choe Tan and others, because Im Yon had rebelled, brought more than fifty cities of the Western Capital to submit.

sentences.zh: 遣斷事官別同瓦馳驛於王綧、洪茶丘所管實科差戶內簽軍至東京，付樞密院，得三千三百人。

translations.literal: The judicial officer Bietongwa was sent by relay post to conscript troops from the actual tax households under Wang Son and Hong Chaqiu's jurisdiction to Dongjing; they were handed to the Privy Council, yielding three thousand three hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial officer Bietongwa was sent by relay post to conscript troops from the tax households under Wang Son and Hong Chaqiu to Dongjing; they were handed to the Privy Council, yielding three thousand three hundred men.

sentences.zh: 高麗西京都統李延齡乞益兵，遣忙哥都率兵二千赴之。

translations.literal: The Goryeo Western Capital commander Li Yanling requested additional troops; Monggedu was sent leading two thousand men to join him.
translations.idiomatic: The Goryeo Western Capital commander Li Yanling requested reinforcements; Monggedu was sent with two thousand troops to join him.

sentences.zh: 樞密院臣議征高麗事。

translations.literal: Privy Council members deliberated on campaigning against Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Privy Council members deliberated on campaigning against Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 初，馬亨以為「高麗者，本箕子所封之地，漢、晉皆為郡縣。

translations.literal: Initially Ma Heng held that "Goryeo was originally the land enfeoffed to Jizi; under Han and Jin it was all commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Ma Heng argued that "Goryeo was originally the land enfeoffed to Jizi; under Han and Jin it was all commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 今雖來朝，其心難測。

translations.literal: Now although they come to court, their hearts are hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Now although they come to court, their intentions are hard to fathom.

sentences.zh: 莫若嚴兵假道，以取日本為名，乘勢可襲其國，定為郡縣」。

translations.literal: Better to mass troops and request passage under the pretext of taking Japan; seizing the opportunity one can strike their country and fix it as commanderies and counties."
translations.idiomatic: Better to mass troops and request passage under the pretext of taking Japan; seizing the opportunity one can strike their country and reduce it to commanderies and counties."

sentences.zh: 亨又言：「今既有釁端，不宜遣兵伐之。

translations.literal: Heng also said: "Now that there is already a provocation, it is not fitting to send troops to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Heng also said, "Now that there is already a provocation, it is not fitting to send troops to attack them.

sentences.zh: 萬一不勝，上損國威，下損士卒。

translations.literal: If by any chance we do not prevail, above we damage national prestige, below we damage the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: If by any chance we do not prevail, we damage national prestige above and waste soldiers below.

sentences.zh: 彼或上表言情，宜赦其罪戾，減其貢獻，以安撫其民，庶幾感慕聖化。

translations.literal: If they submit a memorial pleading their case, their crimes should be pardoned and their tribute reduced, to soothe their people—then perhaps they may be moved to admire the sacred transformation.
translations.idiomatic: If they submit a memorial pleading their case, their crimes should be pardoned and their tribute reduced to soothe their people—then perhaps they may be moved to admire imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 俟南宋已平，彼有他志，回兵誅之，亦未晚也。

translations.literal: Wait until Southern Song is pacified; if they harbor other designs, wheel the army back to punish them—it will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until Southern Song is pacified; if they harbor other designs, wheel the army back to punish them—it will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 」前樞密院經歷馬希驥亦言：「今之高麗，乃古新羅、百濟、高句麗三國併而為一。

translations.literal: " The former Privy Council administrator Ma Xiji also said: "Present-day Goryeo is the merger of the three ancient states of Silla, Baekje, and Goguryeo into one.
translations.idiomatic: " The former Privy Council administrator Ma Xiji also said, "Present-day Goryeo is the merger of the three ancient states of Silla, Baekje, and Goguryeo into one.

sentences.zh: 大抵藩鎮權分則易制，諸侯強盛則難臣。

translations.literal: In general, when frontier powers are divided authority is easy to control; when feudal lords are strong they are hard to subdue.
translations.idiomatic: In general, when frontier powers are divided authority is easy to control; when feudal lords are strong they are hard to subdue.

sentences.zh: 驗彼州城軍民多寡，離而為二，分治其國，使權侔勢等，自相維制，則徐議良圖，亦易為區處耳。

translations.literal: Examine the numbers of their prefectures, cities, soldiers, and civilians; divide them in two and govern the country separately, making powers and strengths equal so they restrain one another—then one may slowly deliberate a good plan, and disposition will also be easy.
translations.idiomatic: Examine the numbers of their prefectures, cities, soldiers, and civilians; divide the country in two and govern it separately, making powers equal so they restrain one another—then one may slowly deliberate a good plan, and disposition will also be easy.

sentences.zh: 」黑的等至其國，禃受詔復位，遣借禮部侍郎朴烋從黑的等奉表入朝。

translations.literal: " When Hei Di and the others reached their country, Chung received the edict and was restored; he sent acting Vice Minister of Rites Bak Hyu with Hei Di and the others presenting a memorial to court.
translations.idiomatic: " When Hei Di and the others reached Goryeo, Chung received the edict and was restored; he sent acting Vice Minister of Rites Bak Hyu to court with a memorial, following Hei Di.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乃親朝京師。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he came in person to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he came in person to the capital.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，遣使言：「比奉詔，臣已復位，令從七百人入覲。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year envoys were sent saying: "Recently, having received the edict, I have been restored and was ordered to bring seven hundred men to audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year envoys were sent saying, "Recently, having received the edict, I have been restored and was ordered to bring seven hundred men to audience.

sentences.zh: 」詔令從四百人來，餘留之西京。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered that four hundred men should come; the rest were to remain in the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered that four hundred men should come; the rest were to remain in the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 詔西京內屬，改東寧府，畫慈悲嶺為界，以忙哥都為安撫使，佩虎符，率兵戍其西境。

translations.literal: An edict made the Western Capital an inner subject, changing it to Dongning Prefecture; Cibei Ridge was drawn as the boundary; Monggedu was made pacification commissioner, wearing the tiger tally, leading troops to garrison its western border.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made the Western Capital an inner subject, renaming it Dongning Prefecture; Cibei Ridge was drawn as the boundary; Monggedu was made pacification commissioner with the tiger tally, leading troops to garrison the western border.

sentences.zh: 詔諭其國僚屬軍民以討林衍之故，其略曰：「朕即位以來，閔爾國久罹兵亂，冊定爾主，撤還兵戍，十年之間，其所以撫護安全者，靡所不至。

translations.literal: An edict instructed the officials, soldiers, and people of their country on account of the campaign against Im Yon; the gist was: "Since my accession I have pitied that your country long suffered military disorder; I enfeoffed and fixed your lord, withdrew the garrison troops, and in ten years there has been no measure of soothing protection and security I have not applied.
translations.idiomatic: An edict instructed the officials, soldiers, and people of Goryeo on account of the campaign against Im Yon, saying in substance: "Since my accession I have pitied that your country long suffered military disorder; I enfeoffed and confirmed your king, withdrew the garrison troops, and in ten years there has been no measure of protection I have not applied.

sentences.zh: 不圖逆臣林衍自作弗靖，擅廢易國王禃，脅立安慶公淐，詔令赴闕，復稽延不出，豈可釋而不誅。

translations.literal: I did not expect that the rebellious minister Im Yon would himself create disorder, on his own authority deposing and replacing King Chung, coercing the installation of the Duke of Anqing Cheo; when an edict ordered him to come to court he again delayed and would not come out—how can he be released without punishment?
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect that the rebellious minister Im Yon would himself create disorder, on his own authority deposing King Chung and coercing the installation of the Duke of Anqing Cheo; when an edict ordered him to court he again delayed and would not come—how can he be released without punishment?

sentences.zh: 已遣行省率兵東下，惟林衍一身是討。

translations.literal: I have already sent the Secretariat leading troops east; only Im Yon's person is to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: I have already sent the Secretariat leading troops east; only Im Yon himself is to be punished.

sentences.zh: 其安慶公淐本非得已，在所寬宥。

translations.literal: The Duke of Anqing Cheo himself was not doing this willingly and is to be broadly pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Anqing Cheo himself acted under compulsion and is to be broadly pardoned.

sentences.zh: 自餘脅從詿誤，一無所問。

translations.literal: As for the rest who were coerced or misled, nothing is to be asked of them.
translations.idiomatic: As for the rest who were coerced or misled, nothing is to be asked of them.

sentences.zh: 」二月，遣軍送禃就國，詔諭高麗國官吏軍民曰：「朕惟臣之事君，有死無二，不意爾國權臣，輒敢擅廢國主。

translations.literal: In the second month troops were sent escorting Chung to his country; an edict instructed the officials, soldiers, and people of Goryeo, saying: "I consider that a subject's service to his lord is death without duplicity; I did not expect powerful ministers of your country to dare on their own authority to depose the king."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month troops were sent escorting Chung home; an edict instructed Goryeo's officials, soldiers, and people: "I hold that a subject serves his lord unto death without duplicity; I did not expect your country's powerful ministers to dare depose the king on their own authority."

sentences.zh: 彼既驅率兵衆，將致爾衆危擾不安，以汝黎庶之故，特遣兵護送國王禃還國，奠居舊京，命達魯花赤同往鎮撫，以靖爾邦。

translations.literal: Since they have driven and led troops and will bring danger and unrest to your masses, for the sake of you, the common people, I specially send troops to escort King Chung back, to settle him in the old capital, and order darughachi to go together to pacify and soothe, to bring calm to your state.
translations.idiomatic: Because they have led troops and will bring danger and unrest to your people, for your sake I specially send troops to escort King Chung home, restore him in the old capital, and order darughachi to go with him to pacify your state.

sentences.zh: 惟爾東土之人，不知為汝之故，必生疑懼，爾衆咸當無畏，按堵如故。

translations.literal: Only you people of the eastern land, not knowing it is for your sake, will surely grow suspicious and fearful—you should all be without fear and live in peace as before.
translations.idiomatic: You people of the east, not knowing this is for your sake, may grow fearful—you should all be without fear and live in peace as before.

sentences.zh: 已別敕將帥，嚴戒兵士勿令侵犯。

translations.literal: I have separately charged the generals strictly to forbid soldiers from invading.
translations.idiomatic: I have separately charged the generals strictly to forbid the soldiers from invading.

sentences.zh: 汝或妄動，汝妻子及汝身當致俘略，宜審思之。」

translations.literal: If you rashly stir, your wives and children and your own person will be taken captive—think carefully."
translations.idiomatic: If you rashly stir, your wives, children, and your own persons will be taken captive—think carefully."

sentences.zh: 初，有旨令頭輦哥行省駐西京，而以忙哥都、趙良弼充安撫使，與禃俱入其京；

translations.literal: Initially there was an order that Tounaige's Secretariat should station at the Western Capital, while Monggedu and Zhao Liangbi would serve as pacification commissioners and enter the capital with Chung;
translations.idiomatic: Initially there was an order that Tounaige's Secretariat should station at the Western Capital, while Monggedu and Zhao Liangbi would serve as pacification commissioners and enter the capital with Chung;

sentences.zh: 既而復令行省入其王京，而以脫朶兒充其國達魯花赤，罷安撫司。

translations.literal: later it was again ordered that the Secretariat should enter the royal capital, while Tuoduo'er would serve as darughachi of their country and the Pacification Office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: later it was ordered that the Secretariat should enter the royal capital, while Tuoduo'er would serve as the country's darughachi and the Pacification Office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 四月，東京行尚書省軍近西京，遣徹徹都等同禃之臣鄭子璵等持省劄召高麗國令公林衍。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the army of the Eastern Capital Secretariat advanced near the Western Capital; Chechedu and others together with Chung's subject Jeong Jau held provincial orders summoning Goryeo State Duke Im Yon.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the Eastern Capital Secretariat army advanced near the Western Capital; Chechedu and others, with Chung's subject Jeong Jau, carried provincial orders summoning Goryeo State Duke Im Yon.

sentences.zh: 使還，言：「衍已死，子惟茂襲令公位。

translations.literal: The envoys returned saying: "Yon is already dead; his son Yuimao has succeeded to the State Duke position.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys returned saying, "Yon is already dead; his son Yuimao has succeeded to the State Duke position.

sentences.zh: 其國侍郎洪文系、尚書宋宗禮，殺惟茂及衍壻崔宗紹。

translations.literal: Their Vice Minister Hong Munyeol and Minister Song Jongni killed Yuimao and Yon's son-in-law Choe Jongso.
translations.idiomatic: Their Vice Minister Hong Munyeol and Minister Song Jongni killed Yuimao and Yon's son-in-law Choe Jongso.

sentences.zh: 惟茂弟惟裀自剄。

translations.literal: Yuimao's younger brother Yuin slit his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: Yuimao's younger brother Yuin slit his own throat.

sentences.zh: 衍黨裴仲孫等復集餘衆，立禃庶族承化侯為王，竄入珍島。

translations.literal: Yon's faction Pei Zhongsun and others again gathered remnant troops, set up Chung's collateral the Marquis of Seonghwa as king, and fled into Jin Island.
